content: 1. For neonates with a birth weight between 2 and 5 kilograms, administer nevirapine at a dose of 8 mg orally. For neonates with a birth weight greater than 2 kilograms, administer 12 mg orally. Administer three doses during the first week of life: the first dose 48 hours after birth, the second dose 48 hours after the first dose, and the third dose 96 hours after the second dose. This regimen is recommended in combination with six weeks of zidovudine therapy. 2. The 14-day lead-in period with immediate-release dosing of nevirapine must be strictly followed, as it has been shown to reduce the frequency of rash. If nevirapine extended-release therapy is interrupted for more than seven days, restart with the lead-in dosing using immediate-release nevirapine. 3. If a mild-to-moderate rash (without systemic symptoms) occurs during the 14-day lead-in period, do not increase the immediate-release dose or initiate the extended-release regimen until the rash resolves. The lead-in dosing period should not exceed 28 days; if the rash persists, an alternative regimen should be chosen. 4. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in reduced serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. 5. Carbamazepine decreases nevirapine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to a loss of virologic response and potential resistance to NNRTIs. 6. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. CYP3A4 is responsible for the formation and elimination of cariprazine's active metabolites, and the effect of CYP3A4 inducers on cariprazine exposure has not been fully evaluated. 7. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers may reduce cobimetinib systemic exposure by more than 80%, significantly reducing its efficacy. 8. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest as a contraceptive while taking strong CYP3A4 inducers due to reduced contraceptive efficacy. Estradiol valerate/dienogest should not be used for at least 28 days after discontinuation of the inducer. 9. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of doravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to reduced doravirine plasma concentrations, loss of virologic response, and potential resistance to doravirine. 10. Both efavirenz and nevirapine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Co-administration is contraindicated, as this combination is associated with increased adverse reactions without improved efficacy. 11. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may reduce the therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir. 12. Nevirapine should not be co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, as this combination is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be used with other antiretrovirals. 13. Nevirapine decreases the levels of etravirine by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Manufacturer's prescribing information advises against combining etravirine with other NNRTIs. 14. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, as it may reduce ivacaftor exposure by 57%, potentially decreasing the effectiveness of the combination therapy. 15. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in reduced serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. 16. Nevirapine decreases the levels of lurasidone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 18. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may reduce paritaprevir and ritonavir levels, leading to decreased efficacy of the Viekira Pak. 19. Nevirapine decreases the levels of panobinostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce panobinostat levels by approximately 70%, leading to treatment failure. 20. Nevirapine decreases the levels of regorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it decreases regorafenib levels and increases exposure to its active metabolite M-5. 21. Nevirapine decreases the levels of rilpivirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as rilpivirine should not be used in combination with NNRTIs. 22. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of roflumilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, as strong CYP450 enzyme inducers reduce systemic exposure to roflumilast, potentially decreasing its therapeutic effectiveness. 23. Nevirapine decreases the levels of vandetanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as potent CYP3A4 inducers reduce vandetanib exposure by up to 40%. 24. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration is necessary, dose adjustments may be required. 25. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If a strong CYP3A4 inducer must be used, increase the acalabrutinib dose to 200 mg twice daily. 26. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of nevirapine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration is necessary, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 27. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of apremilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP inducers significantly reduces systemic exposure to apremilast, potentially resulting in loss of efficacy. 28. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Nevirapine decreases the levels of axitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 30. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 31. Nevirapine decreases the levels of bosutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used, as strong CYP3A4 inducers reduce bosutinib plasma concentration by approximately 85%. 32. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 33. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. If a strong CYP3A4 inducer is required, increase the cabozantinib dose accordingly and resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuation of the inducer. 34. Nevirapine decreases the levels of ceritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 35. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 36. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 37. Nevirapine decreases the levels of dabrafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 38. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used, as it may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance. 39. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of deflazacort by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 40. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 42. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 43. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended due to increased adverse reactions without improved efficacy. 44. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 45. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 46. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ergotamine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 47. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 48. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 49. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of everolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 50. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used.
